findings.body:
`middleware.RequireRole("admin")` previously wrapped both admin handlers; this change registers bare `http.HandlerFunc`s on the v2 subrouter. Unauthenticated or non-admin callers can now hit `GET /api/v2/admin/users` and `POST /api/v2/admin/roles` — listing users and mutating roles with no role gate.

Restore admin enforcement on the subrouter or each route:

```suggestion
	v2.Handle("/admin/users", authz(http.HandlerFunc(a.listUsers))).Methods("GET")
	v2.Handle("/admin/roles", authz(http.HandlerFunc(a.editRoles))).Methods("POST")
```

(with `authz := middleware.RequireRole("admin")` retained above). `v2.Use(middleware.RequireRole("admin"))` is equivalent if every route on this subrouter is admin-only.

summary:
## Verdict

Critical security regression: admin role enforcement was removed while relocating routes under `/api/v2`.

## Narrative

The PathPrefix move to `/api/v2` is reasonable versioning cleanup, but the same hunk drops `middleware.RequireRole("admin")` and registers `listUsers` / `editRoles` as bare handlers. Any client that can reach the process can call `GET /api/v2/admin/users` and `POST /api/v2/admin/roles` with no admin role check.

This tree has no other auth on those handlers (no handler bodies, no router-wide middleware elsewhere), so the removed route wrap was the only visible authorization gate. Restore it on the v2 subrouter — `authz := middleware.RequireRole("admin")` wrapping each handle, or `v2.Use(middleware.RequireRole("admin"))` if every route on that subrouter is admin-only.

The path shift (`/admin/...` → `/api/v2/admin/...`) is an intentional public API break for versioning; consumers need updated paths or deprecated aliases. That is expected and secondary to the authz drop.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The patch removed `middleware.RequireRole("admin")` and now mounts `listUsers`/`editRoles` as bare HandlerFuncs on `/api/v2/admin/*`, with no other RequireRole or auth middleware elsewhere in the tree. This is a real critical authz regression.
